label: Acts 19:1
text: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul, having passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples.

label: Acts 19:2
text: He said to them, “Did you receive the Holy Spirit when you believed?” They said to him, “No, we haven’t even heard that there is a Holy Spirit.”

label: Acts 19:3
text: He said, “Into what then were you baptized?” They said, “Into John’s baptism.”

label: Acts 19:4
text: Paul said, “John indeed baptized with the baptism of repentance, saying to the people that they should believe in the one who would come after him, that is, in Jesus.”

label: Acts 19:5
text: When they heard this, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus.

label: Acts 19:6
text: When Paul had laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.

label: Acts 19:7
text: They were about twelve men in all.

label: Acts 19:8
text: He entered into the synagogue, and spoke boldly for a period of three months, reasoning and persuading about the things concerning God’s Kingdom.

label: Acts 19:9
text: But when some were hardened and disobedient, speaking evil of the Way before the multitude, he departed from them, and separated the disciples, reasoning daily in the school of Tyrannus.

label: Acts 19:10
text: This continued for two years, so that all those who lived in Asia heard the word of the Lord Jesus, both Jews and Greeks.

label: Acts 19:11
text: God worked special miracles by the hands of Paul,

label: Acts 19:12
text: so that even handkerchiefs or aprons were carried away from his body to the sick, and the diseases departed from them, and the evil spirits went out.

label: Acts 19:13
text: But some of the itinerant Jews, exorcists, took on themselves to invoke over those who had the evil spirits the name of the Lord Jesus, saying, “We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.”

label: Acts 19:14
text: There were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.

label: Acts 19:15
text: The evil spirit answered, “Jesus I know, and Paul I know, but who are you?”

label: Acts 19:16
text: The man in whom the evil spirit was leaped on them, overpowered them, and prevailed against them, so that they fled out of that house naked and wounded.

label: Acts 19:17
text: This became known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who lived at Ephesus. Fear fell on them all, and the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.

label: Acts 19:18
text: Many also of those who had believed came, confessing, and declaring their deeds.

label: Acts 19:19
text: Many of those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all. They counted their price, and found it to be fifty thousand pieces of silver.

label: Acts 19:20
text: So the word of the Lord was growing and becoming mighty.

variants.reading: του κυριου ο λογος ('the word of the Lord')
variants.note: The fetched Wikipedia 'Textual variants in the Acts of the Apostles' lists Acts 19:20 του κυριου ο λογος for א, A and B - the reading both graph codices carry. Against it, ο λογος του κυριου is listed for the majority text and η πιστις του κυριου ('the faith of the Lord') for D and syr p 2. The WEB prints the 'word of the Lord' wording.

label: Acts 19:21
text: Now after these things had ended, Paul determined in the spirit, when he had passed through Macedonia and Achaia, to go to Jerusalem, saying, “After I have been there, I must also see Rome.”

label: Acts 19:22
text: Having sent into Macedonia two of those who served him, Timothy and Erastus, he himself stayed in Asia for a while.

label: Acts 19:23
text: About that time there arose no small stir concerning the Way.

label: Acts 19:24
text: For a certain man named Demetrius, a silversmith, who made silver shrines of Artemis, brought no little business to the craftsmen,

label: Acts 19:25
text: whom he gathered together, with the workmen of like occupation, and said, “Sirs, you know that by this business we have our wealth.

label: Acts 19:26
text: You see and hear, that not at Ephesus alone, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul has persuaded and turned away many people, saying that they are no gods, that are made with hands.

label: Acts 19:27
text: Not only is there danger that this our trade come into disrepute, but also that the temple of the great goddess Artemis will be counted as nothing, and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worships.”

label: Acts 19:28
text: When they heard this they were filled with anger, and cried out, saying, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

label: Acts 19:29
text: The whole city was filled with confusion, and they rushed with one accord into the theater, having seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul’s companions in travel.

label: Acts 19:30
text: When Paul wanted to enter in to the people, the disciples didn’t allow him.

label: Acts 19:31
text: Certain also of the Asiarchs, being his friends, sent to him and begged him not to venture into the theater.

label: Acts 19:32
text: Some therefore cried one thing, and some another, for the assembly was in confusion. Most of them didn’t know why they had come together.

label: Acts 19:33
text: They brought Alexander out of the multitude, the Jews putting him forward. Alexander beckoned with his hand, and would have made a defense to the people.

label: Acts 19:34
text: But when they perceived that he was a Jew, all with one voice for a time of about two hours cried out, “Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!”

label: Acts 19:35
text: When the town clerk had quieted the multitude, he said, “You men of Ephesus, what man is there who doesn’t know that the city of the Ephesians is temple keeper of the great goddess Artemis, and of the image which fell down from Zeus?

label: Acts 19:36
text: Seeing then that these things can’t be denied, you ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rash.

label: Acts 19:37
text: For you have brought these men here, who are neither robbers of temples nor blasphemers of your goddess.

label: Acts 19:38
text: If therefore Demetrius and the craftsmen who are with him have a matter against anyone, the courts are open, and there are proconsuls. Let them press charges against one another.

label: Acts 19:39
text: But if you seek anything about other matters, it will be settled in the regular assembly.

label: Acts 19:40
text: For indeed we are in danger of being accused concerning today’s riot, there being no cause. Concerning it, we wouldn’t be able to give an account of this commotion.”

label: Acts 19:41
text: When he had thus spoken, he dismissed the assembly.

label: Apollos
note: Alexandrian Jew learned in the scriptures, instructed in the way of the Lord, active at Corinth while Paul was at Ephesus (Acts 18:24-19:1). No source outside the New Testament names him.

label: Ephesus
note: Principal city of the Roman province of Asia; Paul's base for over two years (Acts 19:8-10).

label: Ephesus (Ephesos) archaeological site
excavators: John Turtle Wood (1863-1869); Otto Benndorf; Austrian Archaeological Institute and Turkish Museum excavations from 1895
note: Excavated since 1863-1869; UNESCO World Heritage Site (2015). The city moved its location as the Cayster river silted the harbour.

label: Temple of Artemis (Artemision), Ephesus
excavators: John Turtle Wood (rediscovered 1869; British Museum excavations)
periods: Archaic (7th century BC) to Roman; destroyed 262 AD, final destruction c. 401 AD
note: One of the Seven Wonders of the Ancient World; only foundations and a single reconstructed column remain in situ.

label: Great Theatre of Ephesus
excavators: Excavated with the city site (Austrian Archaeological Institute)
periods: Hellenistic, rebuilt and enlarged in the Roman imperial period
note: Open-air theatre with an estimated 25,000 seating capacity, believed the largest in the ancient world; used for drama, later gladiatorial combats.

label: Salutaris foundation inscription, Ephesus (I.Ephesos 27)
date: 104 CE (dated by the eprytanis to the consulships of Sex. Attius Suburanus II and M. Asinius Marcellus)
note: C. Vibius Salutaris's foundation decree: silver images of Artemis and of the Roman emperors carried in procession from the temple of Artemis to the theatre on fixed occasions, including the twelve sacred and regular assembly meetings fixed by law and custom.

label: Edict of Paullus Fabius Persicus, proconsul of Asia, on the Artemision
note: The proconsul of Asia reforms the temple of Artemis's finances and priesthoods; the province of Asia was as a rule governed by proconsuls staying in office only a year.

label: Ephesian inscription of the association of silversmiths (argyrokopoi)
note: Refers to 'the association of silversmiths' (to synderion ton argyrokopon), confirming such a guild existed at Ephesus.

label: Ephesian official documents dated by the grammateus
note: The grammateus (town clerk) was among the most prominent civic officials of Ephesus; his name was used to date official documents found in the city.

label: Civic coins of Ephesus titled neokoros ('temple keeper')
date: Roman imperial era (the illustrated Elagabalus-era coin reads 'alone of all, four times neokoros')
note: Ephesus's civic coinage proudly carried the neokoros title; the title for Ephesus as guardian of the Artemision is attested in inscriptions and on coins.

label: Inscriptions naming Asiarchs of the province of Asia
found: cities of Asia, including Ephesus and Pergamon
note: Asiarchs were elected by the cities and confirmed by the Roman proconsul; they organized the provincial koinon's games and imperial-cult festivals.

label: Statues of Artemis of Ephesus (the 'Lady of Ephesus')
date: 1st-2nd century CE copies of the cult image
held_at: Ephesus Archaeological Museum; National Archaeological Museum, Naples (Farnese Artemis)
note: Many marble copies of the Ephesian goddess survive, including the 1st-century Artemis statue and 2nd-century 'Lady of Ephesus' in the Ephesus Archaeological Museum and the Farnese Artemis in Naples.

label: Proconsular edict on a bakers' riot, Magnesia on the Maeander
note: Records a riot provoked by a guild of bakers, using words for disturbance, tumult and sedition closely resembling the vocabulary of Acts 19.

label: Inscription from Himera with the Ephesia grammata formula
date: before 409 BC (before the Carthaginian destruction of Himera)
note: A damaged inscription apparently attesting a version of the six-word Ephesian magical formula; the formula reappears on magical papyri through the Hellenistic period.

label: Apollos was at Corinth while Paul came to Ephesus
statement: While Apollos was at Corinth, Paul passed through the upper country and came to Ephesus.

label: Paul came to Ephesus and found disciples
statement: Paul passed through the upper country, came to Ephesus, and found certain disciples there.

label: About twelve Ephesian disciples had received only John's baptism and were baptized into the name of the Lord Jesus
statement: Disciples at Ephesus told Paul they had not received the Holy Spirit and had been baptized into John's baptism; after Paul explained, they were baptized in the name of the Lord Jesus. They were about twelve men in all.

label: The Holy Spirit came on the twelve, who spoke in tongues and prophesied
statement: When Paul laid his hands on them, the Holy Spirit came on them, and they spoke with other languages and prophesied.
note: Miracle claim; none-found in every external category.

label: Paul reasoned three months in the Ephesus synagogue
statement: Paul entered the synagogue at Ephesus and spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and persuading about the kingdom of God.

label: Paul taught daily for two years in the school (lecture hall) of Tyrannus
statement: When some opposed the Way, Paul withdrew, separated the disciples, and reasoned daily for two years in the school of Tyrannus, so that all who lived in Asia, Jews and Greeks, heard the word.
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: Handkerchiefs and aprons carried from Paul healed the sick and expelled evil spirits
statement: God worked special miracles by Paul's hands, so that handkerchiefs or aprons carried from his body to the sick drove out diseases and evil spirits.
note: Miracle claim; none-found in every external category.

label: Itinerant Jewish exorcists adjured the possessed by powerful names
statement: Itinerant Jewish exorcists took it on themselves to invoke over the possessed the name of the Lord Jesus, saying 'We adjure you by Jesus whom Paul preaches.'

label: Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, had seven sons who practiced this exorcism
statement: Seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, were doing this.

label: The possessed man overpowered the seven sons, who fled naked and wounded
statement: The evil spirit answered that it knew Jesus and Paul but not them; the possessed man leaped on the seven sons, overpowered them, and they fled the house naked and wounded.
note: Miracle claim; none-found in every external category.

label: Ephesian converts burned their magic books publicly, worth 50,000 pieces of silver
statement: Many who had believed confessed their deeds, and those who practiced magical arts brought their books together and burned them in the sight of all; the price was counted at fifty thousand pieces of silver.

label: Magical books and formulas were a known feature of Ephesus and the region
statement: Ephesus was a place where magical arts were practiced with books and formulas (the tradition of the Ephesia grammata).

label: Paul planned to pass through Macedonia and Achaia to Jerusalem and then Rome, and sent Timothy and Erastus ahead
statement: Paul resolved to pass through Macedonia and Achaia and go to Jerusalem, saying he must also see Rome; he sent Timothy and Erastus into Macedonia and stayed in Asia a while.

label: Demetrius, a silversmith, made silver shrines of Artemis
statement: Demetrius, a silversmith, made silver shrines of Artemis and brought no little business to the craftsmen.

label: Miniature silver shrines of Artemis were manufactured and sold in Ephesus
statement: Silver shrines (naoi) of Artemis were manufactured and sold in Ephesus, providing wealth for the silversmiths and craftsmen.

label: The temple of the great goddess Artemis stood at Ephesus
statement: The temple of the great goddess Artemis was at Ephesus and was her celebrated sanctuary.

label: The Artemis cult spread through the province of Asia and beyond
statement: The Artemis of Ephesus was venerated 'throughout all Asia' and beyond - Paul's teaching that gods made with hands are not gods had turned away many across the province.

label: Crowds acclaimed Artemis with the shout 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!'
statement: The crowd cried out for about two hours with one voice, 'Great is Artemis of the Ephesians!' (megale he Artemis Ephesion).

label: The crowd gathered in the theater of Ephesus
statement: The whole city rushed with one accord into the theater, which served as the meeting place of the citizen assembly.
note: Kind corrected from place to event in consolidation B: the statement is an event (the matrix anchors office/event/object/custom/time claims).

label: Gaius and Aristarchus, Macedonian companions of Paul, were seized
statement: The crowd seized Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's companions in travel.

label: Asiarchs of Asia, some Paul's friends, urged Paul not to enter the theater
statement: Certain of the Asiarchs - leading figures of the province of Asia connected with the imperial cult and the provincial games - being Paul's friends, sent word begging him not to venture into the theater. The disciples also barred him.

label: Alexander, put forward by the Jews, attempted to address the crowd

statement: The town clerk (grammateus), one of Ephesus's most senior civic officials, quieted the crowd and addressed the assembly.

label: Ephesus held the title neokoros, temple keeper of great Artemis
statement: The town clerk declared that the city of the Ephesians was temple keeper (neokoros) of the great goddess Artemis.

statement: The town clerk referred to the image of Artemis which fell down from Zeus - a sky-fallen (diopetes) cult image.
